newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to launch film production support program.
newsitem.headline: Canada to launch film production support program.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Wednesday it plans a new financial support program for film and video production, which for the first time would make funding available to Hollywood studios.
Unlike past funding programs, which applied only to Canadian productions, the new program will be available to both domestic and foreign producers shooting in Canada.
Government officials -- who would not reveal how much the program will be worth -- said it would consult with the industry to decide what form the program should take.
"The details haven't been worked out," Ed Short, a tax policy officer with the Canadian Finance Department, told Reuters.
"We could go with a tax credit that's given directly to the producer or we could go with a grant directly to the film producer, or perhaps by low interest loans," Short said.
The new program will be tied to the labor expenses of productions and take effect in November.

Historically, the Canadian government has provided direct financial support only to productions that met certain "Canadian content" requirements. The requirements included having a percentage of Canadians involved in both the creative and financial components of the film.
That included films such as David Cronenberg's "Crash", Atom Egoyan's "Exotica" and "The Sweet Hereafter" and Lynne Stopkewich's "Kissed".
Government officials acknowledged the new program was designed partly to lure foreign productions to Canada.

"It's expected that it could be used by Hollywood studios in Canada and that's not necessarily a bad thing. The idea behind this is to promote jobs," said Short. "The idea is to try to bring some of those jobs to Canada."
In 1996 foreign film and television production in Canada exceeded C$800 million (US$580 million). Many producers are lured to Canada by the weak currency and skilled crews.
Toronto is the third largest film and televison production center in North America after Los Angeles and New York.
